test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

**Statements:**

All Cabbages are Peas.

No Peas are Broccolis.

**Conclusions:**

I: No Broccolis are Cabbages.

II: Some Broccolis are Cabbages.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12b40783ab85a5918847b6e55c6bc06375539e3c2ac72f896c1beb10e88aa787.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/712b9afaef6d1c4ad25c2958068979a2ef506bb5c6e8e45200d40a674f999867.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No Broccolis are Cabbages → Follow (As all Cabbages are Peas and no Peas are Broccolis. As whole cabbages comes in peas which cannot be broccolis, therefore it is true.)

II. Some Broccolis are Cabbages → Does not follow (As all Cabbages are Peas and no Peas are Broccolis. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
